new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (6 pp. the PDF's metadata gives the Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-08-24). extracted text of PDF page 5 (running header 'Kire (Giri) OPD Printed: August 25, 2004 Page 5') gives, between the vowel-cluster table and 'Syllable Patterns', exactly two lines: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Stress is probably phonemic.' Verbatim match to the reported quote. I read all six pages: no other mention of stress, accent, tone or length; the wordlist examples, syllable-pattern list and the transcribed passage on p.6 carry no stress marks; the bibliography is the single item 'Pryor, David and Sharran. Kire Phonology and Orthography. Manuscript. SIL, Ukarumpa.' Reading: the senten…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only published statement is a one-line hedge: stress is 'probably phonemic', i.e. the analysts thought stress placement is contrastive/not predictable by rule, but they give no rule, no default position and no minimal pairs. Nothing on tone or length is claimed either. A 'lexical (unpredictable)' reading is the best fit to the words but rests on a single hedged sentence.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level implied (an OPD 'Suprasegmentals' line on phonemic status); no domain, examples, or minimal pairs given. Stress is not marked in the wordlist examples or the transcribed passage.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Kire (Giri) Language [GEB], Madang Province; Sepik-Ramu Phylum; Ramu Super-Stock; Misegian Family; major villages Giri 1 and 2, Tung, Birap' — the same variety as kire1240 (Wikipedia/Glottolog locate Kire at Giri village); no dialect split is described. 'Giri' is Z'graggen's name for the same language; Stanhope's 'Kire people, Bogia' is the same community.

Typological Features of the Ruboni Stock 1) Stops are found at at least three points of articulation ... 3) Fricatives have been observed at three points of articulation: labio-dental, alveolar and velar. The /f/ and /z/ phonemes have not been observed in Ottilien. The /h/ phoneme is present in Giri and perhaps in Mikarew. ... 5) Unrounded vowels are found in front and low-central positions, rounded vowels in back positions and a high central vowel type has been observed in all members except in Kaian and Gamei. 6) None of the languages appears to be tonal. 7) Number marking is present with nouns.
